title: Magyar Meets Von der Leyen and Costa in Brussels — EU Funds Deal Targeted for Late May
detail: Incoming Prime Minister Péter Magyar traveled to Brussels on April 29, 2026 for direct meetings with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa. The meetings were described as 'constructive and productive' by both sides. Magyar confirmed that he would return to Brussels in the week of May 25 to conclude the formal political agreement necessary to unlock approximately €17 billion in frozen EU funds. The discussions covered the 27 'super milestones' Hungary must fulfill — including judicial independence reforms, anti-corruption measures, EPPO membership, and public procurement transparency — before the EU can begin disbursing the funds. The August 31, 2026 deadline for the €10.4B Recovery and Resilience Facility tranche created strong mutual incentive for a swift conclusion. Von der Leyen praised Magyar's 'clear commitment to European values and the rule of law' and expressed confidence that an agreement would be reached before the deadline. This was Magyar's first formal engagement at European Commission presidential level.

media.caption: Magyar meets von der Leyen in Brussels to discuss unlocking Hungary's €17B in frozen EU funds

title: White House Publishes US-Hungary Bilateral Partnership Fact Sheet — Signals Warmer Ties
detail: The White House published a fact sheet on April 29, 2026 titled 'Advancing the United States-Hungary Bilateral Partnership,' marking a significant shift in US-Hungary relations following Péter Magyar's election victory. The document outlined areas of expanded cooperation including defense, trade, energy security, and democratic governance. The statement represented the Biden administration's endorsement of the transition from Orbán's government, which had been viewed as a persistent outlier in the NATO alliance due to its Russia-aligned posture. Under Orbán, US-Hungary relations had cooled significantly, with Hungary repeatedly blocking NATO consensus on Ukraine. The fact sheet signals that Washington expects Hungary to be a more reliable NATO partner under Magyar and signals US support for the new government's EU integration agenda.

media.caption: White House announces advancement of US-Hungary bilateral partnership following Magyar election

title: Two Additional Gripen Jets Delivered to Kecskemét — Hungary Strengthens NATO Air Posture
detail: Two additional JAS 39C Gripen fighter jets arrived at Kecskemét Air Base on April 29, 2026, fulfilling a February 2024 order from Swedish manufacturer Saab. The delivery adds to Hungary's existing Gripen fleet and signals the new government's commitment to reinforcing NATO air defense capabilities. The aircraft were ordered under the Orbán government but their arrival under Magyar's transition is being read as a statement of NATO alignment. Hungary is preparing to display a new puma-themed Gripen livery at the NATO Tiger Meet 2026 exercise at Araxos Air Base in Greece (May 4–15). The delivery comes as Magyar's government moves to end the Orbán era's tensions with NATO allies and commits to greater interoperability with the alliance.

media.caption: Hungary Gripen jets arrive at Kecskemét Air Base as new government strengthens NATO posture
